newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenia receiving electricity from Iran - minister.
newsitem.headline: Armenia receiving electricity from Iran - minister.

text.p: Armenia is receiving electricity from Iran which will help secure its energy needs and could provide a source of income for the land-locked state, Armenian Energy Minister Gagik Martirosyan told Reuters in an interview.
He said Armenia was receiving 65.8 megawatts of energy per day, slightly in excess of the 65 megawatts per day supply rate agreed by the two in February.
Repair work on high-voltage lines between Iran and Armenia began in March.
"This is the first serious project since the operation of atomic power stations in Armenia," Martirosyan said.
Officials say the new power supplies reduce Armenia's dependence on its nuclear power plant, and on a natural gas pipeline through Georgia.
Armenia suffered critical shortages of electricity in the early 1990s after the Soviet Union collapsed and Armenia lost its cheap supplies of natural gas from Turkmenistan.
But the shortages eased after Yerevan re-opened the Metsamor Nuclear Power Plant in June 1995 and toughened rules on paying domestic and commercial electricity bills.

Martirosyan said linking Armenia's power grid to Iran's was of strategic importance and would allow electricity to be transported across Armenia to other countries as well as ensuring secure electricity supplies to Armenia.
An agreement to link Armenia's power grid to Iran's was signed in May 1995.
